[WC Docket Nos. 10-90, 26-96, 26-288; FCC No. 26-75; FR ID 378440]
Federal Communications Commission.
In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC or Commission) initiates a rulemaking to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, certain new funding awards of high-cost Universal Service Fund (USF) support.
Comments are due on or before December 23, 2026 and reply comments are due on or before January 22, 2027. If you anticipate that you will be submitting comments but find it difficult to do so within the period of time allowed by this document, you should advise the contact listed in the following as soon as possible.
Pursuant to §§ 1.415 and 1.419 of the Commission's rules, 47 CFR 1.415, 1.419, interested parties may file comments and reply comments on or before the dates indicated in the DATES section of this document. You may submit comments identified by WC Docket Nos. 10-90, 26-96, and 26-288, by any of the following methods:
Electronic Filers: Comments may be filed electronically using the internet by accessing the ECFS: https://www.fcc.gov/​ecfs/​.
Paper Filers: Parties who choose to file by paper must file an original and one copy of each filing.
Filings can be sent by hand or messenger delivery, by commercial courier, or by the U.S. Postal Service. All filings must be addressed to the Secretary, Federal Communications Commission.
Hand-delivered or messenger-delivered paper filings for the Commission's Secretary are accepted between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. by the FCC's mailing contractor at 9050 Junction Drive, Annapolis Junction, MD 20701. All hand deliveries must be held together with rubber bands or fasteners. Any envelopes and boxes must be disposed of before entering the building.
Commercial courier deliveries (any deliveries not by the U.S. Postal Service) ( printed page 75483) must be sent to 9050 Junction Drive, Annapolis Junction, MD 20701.
Filings sent by U.S. Postal Service First-Class Mail, Priority Mail, and Priority Mail Express must be sent to 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554.
People with Disabilities: To request materials in accessible formats for people with disabilities (Braille, large print, electronic files, audio format), send an email to fcc504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer & Governmental Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530.
Scott Lively, scott.lively@fcc.gov, Wireline Competition Bureau, 202-418-7400 or TTY: 202-418-0484. Requests for accommodations should be made as soon as possible in order to allow the agency to satisfy such requests whenever possible. Send an email to fcc504@fcc.gov or call the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau at (202) 418-0530.
This is a synopsis of the Commission's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) in WC Docket Nos. 10-90, 26-96, 26-288; FCC No. 26-75; adopted October 29, 2026 and released October 30, 2026. The full text of this document is available for public inspection during regular business hours at the Commission's headquarters at 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554 or at the following internet address: https://www.fcc.gov/​document/​safeguarding-high-cost-funding-through-effective-applicant-vetting.
Ex Parte Rules. The proceeding this NPRM initiates shall be treated as a “permit-but-disclose” proceeding in accordance with the Commission's ex parte rules. Persons making ex parte presentations must file a copy of any written presentation or a memorandum summarizing any oral presentation within two business days after the presentation (unless a different deadline applicable to the Sunshine period applies). Persons making oral ex parte presentations are reminded that memoranda summarizing the presentation must (1) list all persons attending or otherwise participating in the meeting at which the ex parte presentation was made, and (2) summarize all data presented and arguments made during the presentation. If the presentation consisted in whole or in part of the presentation of data or arguments already reflected in the presenter's written comments, memoranda or other filings in the proceeding, the presenter may provide citations to such data or arguments in his or her prior comments, memoranda, or other filings (specifying the relevant page and/or paragraph numbers where such data or arguments can be found) in lieu of summarizing them in the memorandum. Documents shown or given to Commission staff during ex parte meetings are deemed to be written ex parte presentations and must be filed consistent with rule 1.1206(b). In proceedings governed by rule 1.49(f) or for which the Commission has made available a method of electronic filing, written ex parte presentations and memoranda summarizing oral ex parte presentations, and all attachments thereto, must be filed through the electronic comment filing system available for that proceeding, and must be filed in their native format ( e.g.,.doc, .xml, .ppt, searchable .pdf). Participants in this proceeding should familiarize themselves with the Commission's ex parte rules.
In this document, consistent with the directives of the Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025 (RBPA), the Commission initiates a rulemaking to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, certain new funding awards of high-cost USF support.
With this NPRM, the Commission seeks comment on its proposals for implementing the RBPA, including the Commission's proposed interpretation of the Act's definition of “new covered funding awards” under its universal service rules, and what details and documentation an applicant will be required to provide to the Commission to demonstrate that it has the technical, financial, and operational capabilities to deploy and operate a USF-supported network that will meet program requirements. The Commission also invites comment on implementation of the RBPA's penalty framework for pre-authorization defaults.
In proposing rules to implement RBPA's vetting process and penalties for pre-authorization defaults for future awards of new covered funding, the Commission largely tracks the relevant statutory language. The Commission seeks comment on proposals to implement the statutory language in its rules, generally, and with regard to each specific issue addressed in the following.
The Commission proposes to interpret the statute's definitions of “covered funding” and “new covered funding award” to comprise an award of high-cost support based on an application for funding to support the deployment of a broadband-capable network and the provision of supported services over the network. The Commission seeks comment on the proposal.
The Commission proposes to interpret “application” as used in the RBPA as an application for funding from a specific high-cost mechanism wherein the applicant is required to include information and/or certifications regarding technical, financial, and operational capabilities, including, but not limited to, applications for funding from high-cost mechanisms governed by subpart AA of the Commission's rules. Though the Commission could choose to include an RBPA-compliant vetting process in any future high-cost mechanism, its proposed interpretation of application would not require that of high-cost mechanisms that offer support to a carrier based on its Eligible Telecommunications Carrier (ETC) status and mode of FCC regulation ( i.e., rate-of-return or price cap). The Commission seeks comment on the proposal. The Commission's rules distinguish between high-cost mechanisms that require applications from potential funding recipients and other mechanisms. For example, the rules governing the Alternative-Connect America Cost Model (A-CAM) support mechanism state that a rate-of-return carrier receiving support pursuant to 47 CFR part 54, subparts K (Connect America Fund Broadband Loop Support (CAF-BLS)) or M (High-Cost Loop Support (HCLS)) of the Commission's rules “shall have the opportunity to voluntarily elect, on a state-level basis, to receive Connect America Fund (CAF) A-CAM support as calculated by the A-CAM adopted by the Commission in lieu of support calculated pursuant to subparts K or M.” For rate-of-return carriers that continued receiving support from the CAF-BLS and/or HCLS high-cost mechanism, subparts K and M, respectively, of the Commission's rules detail how the support is calculated, and the information required from the support recipient has nothing to do with demonstrating technical, financial, or operational capabilities or the Commission vetting the recipient. Recipients of these mechanisms are vetted using the ETC designation process, which is not directly tied to receipt of support from any specific high-cost mechanism. In summary, these mechanisms offer support (and in some cases the possibility of electing a different support mechanism) to a class of carriers and do not contemplate an ( printed page 75484) “application” or specific applicant vetting, whereas 47 CFR part 1, subpart AA of the Commission's rules enumerates extensive application requirements for carriers interested in participating in competitive bidding for USF support, and those rules are supplemented by further application requirements for each specific high-cost mechanism that employs competitive bidding.
The Commission further proposes to interpret the phrase “the deployment of a broadband-capable network and the provision of supported services over the network” as clarifying that the statute only applies to awards that include both of the two specified categories of funded activities, with “deployment” referring to construction of a network to serve a previously unserved location or upgrading the network to improve service at an underserved or unserved location and “provision of supported services” referring to maintaining existing service levels at a location. Therefore, funding that is being awarded only to maintain existing service levels would not be considered “covered funding” because it is not funding that supports deployment. Further, the Commission proposes that any new requirements adopted in this proceeding to establish a vetting process for a “new covered funding award” would not apply to any existing high-cost mechanisms for which the Commission had already adopted rules prior to enactment of the RBPA. The Commission seeks comment on its proposal and potential alternatives.
The Commission proposes adopting a new general Part 54 rule that would require new covered funding awards, offered through a competitive bidding mechanism or otherwise, to include a detailed RBPA-compliant vetting process. The RBPA provides the basic structure for the proposed new rule by directing the Commission to only award funding to applicants that can demonstrate through an initial application sufficient detail and documentation for the Commission to ascertain that the applicant possesses the technical, financial, and operational capabilities, and has a reasonable business plan, to deploy the proposed network and deliver services with the relevant performance characteristics and requirements defined by the Commission and as pledged by the applicant. The Commission seeks comment on the effectiveness of past and existing vetting frameworks and how those prior frameworks can inform the RBPA's vetting requirements for new covered funding awards. However, given that the Commission does not know what form a future mechanism for distributing “new covered funding awards” will take, it seeks comment on avoiding the adoption of a rigid, specific framework that must be used for all new covered funding awards. Instead, the Commission tentatively concludes that it is sufficient to require that future new covered funding awards meet the basic requirements of the RBPA. Specific requirements for evaluating applications for such new covered funding awards would instead be proposed and adopted as part of the proceedings to establish the program-specific requirements for such funding.
The plain language of the RBPA applies to an applicant's “initial application” for a new covered funding award, not an application to participate in competitive bidding. In the context of high-cost mechanisms that employ competitive bidding, the Commission seeks comment on whether the long-form application constitutes a winning bidder's “initial application” for a “new covered funding award.”
In the first stage of the Commission's well-established two-stage application process for high-cost mechanisms that use competitive bidding, an entity seeking to participate in the competition must provide information and a series of certifications in a short-form application used by the Commission to determine whether the applicant has the necessary legal, technical, and financial qualifications. A determination that an applicant is qualified to bid based on that application is not a determination of the applicant's eligibility for such support.
After competitive bidding concludes, a winning bidder has a binding obligation to file a timely and sufficient post-auction long-form application before it can be authorized to receive the support associated with its winning bid(s). The long-form application contains more extensive information about the winning bidder's qualifications, funding, and the network it intends to use to meet its public interest obligations and performance requirements, as well as a series of certifications, to demonstrate to the Commission that it is legally, technically, and financially qualified to receive the universal service support associated with its winning bids, which allows for a further in-depth review by the Commission of the winning bidder's qualifications prior to any authorization of support.
The Commission has found that requiring an in-depth review of extensive information only from winning bidders at the long-form stage balances the need to collect essential information from potential auction applicants with administrative efficiency and provides an appropriate screen at the pre-auction stage to ensure serious participation by qualified bidders without being unduly burdensome to potential auction participants. Before there is a known pool of applicants for a given competition, finding the optimal balance between encouraging participation and screening out unqualified applicants is difficult to do with any certainty. The Commission has observed in connection with the use of competitive bidding to award high-cost support “that maximizing the number of qualified participants in the competitive bidding process is likely to improve the overall quality of the process.”
In the interest of facilitating a robust and fulsome discussion of applicant vetting, the Commission seeks comment on whether there are further actions at the short-form application stage that, without contravening the purpose of the two-stage application process, could provide greater insight into an applicant's fitness to participate in competitive bidding for universal service support and its ability to meet the expectations of a support recipient. Would a more thorough application and intense vetting of applicants at the short-form stage prevent unqualified bidders from participating in the auction, and then defaulting prior to authorization, as was seen in the Rural Digital Opportunity Fund (RDOF)? Was that the intent of Congress in enacting the RBPA?
The Commission also seeks comment on whether it should require additional information at the long-form application stage to facilitate the Commission's review of winning bidders applying for new covered funding awards for universal service support. For example, to what extent does the Commission need to obtain information showing a realistic assessment that the provider's plans not only will enable the deployment of a network with the required technical and service capabilities that can be funded from available revenues but also the ability to meet pertinent deadlines specified in the program rules? Does the Commission need more specific and/or detailed information than it has received in the past regarding the provider's plans to address the types of challenges that routinely arise in connection with network deployments, such as weather, permitting, land access, or other considerations? The Commission further seeks comment on whether applicants with less experience providing the service(s) for which ( printed page 75485) support will be awarded, or which must be offered as a condition of support, should be required to undergo a more extensive vetting process. If so, how should the Commission categorize applicants based on experience? Could this framework be informed by the prior practice of creating two categories of applicants, those with at least two years of experience providing a voice, broadband, and/or electric transmission or distribution service and those with less than two? What information should be required for each category of applicant, and at what stage in the process?
The most recent use of competitive bidding for high-cost support (Auction 904) benefited from adapting lessons learned from vetting frameworks used by prior mechanisms and should serve as the starting point for discussion. The RDOF vetting framework is summarized in the following.
Applicants to participate in Auction 904 were required to submit:
Applicant information, including legal classification, jurisdiction of formation, address, contact information, and responsible individual
Information regarding any agreements relating to its participation in the auction
Description of the broadband technology the applicant planned to deploy
Recent audited financials (with more financial statements required from less experienced applicants)
A letter from a qualified bank committing to provide a letter of credit
Various certifications, including certifications regarding:
ETC status, including an acknowledgement that it must be designated as an ETC in the relevant areas prior to being authorized to receive support in those areas
Audited financial statements (applicants with at least two years of operational history that were not audited in the ordinary course of business were allowed to submit unaudited financials and certify that they would submit audited financials at the long-form stage if selected)
Compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements
Financial and technical capability to meet the relevant public interest obligations for each performance tier and latency combination in the geographic areas in which it seeks support
Availability of funds for all project costs that exceed the amount of support to be received for the first two years of its support term
Compliance with the relevant public interest obligations
Access to spectrum, if applicable
Information regarding earth station licenses for satellite technology, if applicable
Prior to being authorized to receive the support already won at auction, each winning bidder in Auction 904 was required to submit during the long-form application process:
Documentation of its designation as an ETC in all areas where it will receive support and ETC certification letter(s) from an officer of the applicant certifying that the ETC designation(s) covers all the areas where the applicant will receive support (submitted with long-form application if ETC designation(s) already obtained or no later than 180 days after the announcement of Auction 904 winning bidders if not yet obtained)
Audited financial statements (if not submitted during the pre-auction short-form process)
A detailed technology and system design description that explains how the design and technologies chosen will meet the relevant performance requirements, including information regarding quality, coverage, voice service, network management, and on-going operations, and a detailed network diagram that is certified by a professional engineer; the engineer must certify that the network is capable of delivering, to at least 95% of the required number of locations in each relevant state, voice and broadband service that meets the requisite performance requirements
A description of how the required construction will be funded in each state, specifying how high-cost support and other funds, if applicable, will be used to complete the project, with financial projections demonstrating that the applicant can cover the necessary debt service payments over the life of any loans
An irrevocable standby letter of credit issued by a qualified bank for each state in which it will be authorized to receive support that covers at least the first year of support to be received for the first-year support term for the state
A letter of credit bankruptcy opinion letter from outside legal counsel regarding the treatment of the letter(s) of credit or its proceeds in a bankruptcy proceeding
Similarly, as explained in this document, where the Commission has used a competitive application process, as opposed to competitive bidding, to award high-cost support to a chosen selectee, it has also used a two-stage application process for a selectee to become authorized to receive support, albeit with the inclusion of more extensive applicant information required at the first phase of the application process. Given the unique circumstances of the Bringing Puerto Rico Together (Uniendo a Puerto Rico) Fund and Connect USVI Fund (PR-USVI Funds) program and because the Commission does not know whether, and if so how, it may choose to implement a competitive application process to award support in a future high-cost program, the Commission seeks comment on what it should consider to be an “initial application” for a “new covered funding award” when using that type of process and the information that applicants should be required to include in the initial application.
For future high-cost programs that do not use a system of competitive bidding or another competitive application process to allocate universal service support, the Commission seeks to develop a record on the appropriate framework and content for an application for a new covered funding award under any such program in order to facilitate vetting of such applications in compliance with the RBPA.
For future high-cost programs covered by the RBPA for which support is not allocated through competitive bidding or another competitive application process, the Commission seeks comment on whether the application process and content used to apply for Auction 904 provide a good starting point for establishing the framework for initial applications for new covered funding awards. The Commission further seeks comment on both the substance and the timing for new covered funding award applications outside of a competitive process. In particular, the Commission seeks comment on whether, and if yes, how, it should modify or build upon the requirements used for Auction 904 to ensure the Commission can sufficiently ascertain an applicant's capabilities and conduct the vetting required under the RBPA. The Commission also seeks comment on whether any of these requirements are overly burdensome or not useful outside of a competitive process and should therefore not be ( printed page 75486) required. Commenters are free to use examples from other programs to inform their positions.
The two-phased RDOF vetting process solicits both (i) information that is probative of applicants' technical, financial, and operational capabilities, as well as (ii) additional information that is typically included in prudent business plans. To the extent that future high-cost support mechanisms subject recipients of new covered funding awards to a similarly detailed vetting process, the Commission seeks comment on whether there is a need to also require a business plan on top of the other required submissions. The Commission seeks comment on whether obtaining a substantial amount of information in vetting processes amounts to a “reasonable business plan” as required by the RBPA even if it is not required as part of a separately-labeled portion of the submission. Using the RDOF vetting process as the starting point for discussion, the Commission invites comment and welcomes proposals regarding what applicants should be required to show, if anything, beyond what was required of RDOF program applicants through the two-phased vetting process.
Under the RBPA, the Commission may only award covered funding to applicants that can demonstrate that they meet the qualifications. The RBPA states that the Commission must evaluate the applicant's proposal against “reasonable and well-established technical, financial, and operational standards, including the technical standards adopted by the Commission in orders of the Commission relating to Establishing the Digital Opportunity Data Collection (WC Docket No. 19-195) (or orders of the Commission relating to modernizing any successor collection) for purposes of entities that must report broadband availability coverage.”
Historically, the Commission did not adopt generally applicable standards and assumptions for reviewing information demonstrating a high-cost support applicant's capability given the fact-intensive, case-by-case nature of the review. The Commission benefits from the expertise of Commission engineers and/or other subject matter experts to discuss network plans with each applicant, including engineers and other specialists that support the applicant's operations and/or assisted with the application. Further, given the broad array of broadband technologies that compete in the communications marketplace and diverse terrain of areas needing service, it is difficult to develop one uniform set of evaluation standards for reviewing all applications and also maintain the principles of technology neutrality cited in the RBPA. The Commission invites comment on whether case-by-case evaluation is most appropriate to ensure that eligibility determinations are made consistently across all applications. The Commission welcomes proposals for a set of technical, financial, and operational standards that could be used for evaluating applicants for new covered funding awards in compliance with the RBPA.
The RBPA specifically references technical standards for entities that must report broadband availability coverage. These standards can be found in the Commission`s rules and in the Commission's published guides designed to support entities that must report broadband availability coverage. For example, providers of fixed wired broadband service must not exceed specific maximum buffer distances (which must include the drop distance) from their aggregation points to their served locations when reporting service availability based on their wired technologies, with specific maximum buffer distances for fiber to the premises and hybrid fiber-coax. Similarly, these rules provide certain factors when modeling terrestrial fixed wireless services, including the geographic coordinates of each base station, “the link budget and a description of the other parameters used in the propagation model, including predicted signal strength” and “receiver heights within a range of four to seven meters.” The Commission invites comment on how, for purposes of evaluating applicant technical capability, it could employ these technical standards when evaluating applicants for new covered funding awards.
Under the RBPA, the Commission must also evaluate the applicant's proposal in light of “the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs.” Myriad state and Federal programs could fall under a broad definition of “other government broadband deployment funding programs.” Compliance with some programs may be relatively easier for the Commission to track than others. It may be harder to elicit information about compliance in other programs, such as those with minimal support for network deployment and some state programs. The Commission seeks comment on interpreting “other government broadband deployment funding programs” to mean those programs depicted in the FCC's Broadband Funding Map.
How can the Commission most efficiently and effectively obtain information from administrators of state and other Federal broadband deployment programs that have records of an applicant's compliance history? Should new participants be penalized for having no program compliance history? How should the Commission weigh an applicant's prior history of abiding by, or failure to comply with, program rules? What if the applicant was able to cure its prior non-compliance? How should defaults on awards under other broadband deployment funding programs be addressed? The Commission invites comment on how best to ensure these criteria are fairly and systematically applied across all applicants. The Commission also proposes and invites comment on requiring applicants to disclose if they have been suspended or debarred from other Federal broadband deployment funding programs or are currently subject to an ongoing suspension and debarment action. The Commission further invites comment on how a potential applicant's suspension or debarment status should affect its eligibility to pursue a new covered funding award.
Regarding the Commission's broadband deployment funding programs, applicants that failed to comply with the obligations of high-cost support are subject to the compliance measures in § 54.320 of the Commission's rules, and failure to comply may trigger further action, including suspension or debarment pursuant to rule § 54.8. The Commission invites comment on whether and how a potential applicant previously subject to a non-compliance action under rule § 54.320 should be encumbered in or prevented from pursuing a new covered funding award. For example, Auction 903 participants that subsequently defaulted on their entire award were barred from participating in Auction 904. Should potential applicants that previously substantially defaulted in a universal service program be barred from participating in future competitions for new covered funding awards? How would the Commission determine what constitutes a substantial default, or would it evaluate that default on a case-by-case basis? Should a substantial or complete default result in a ban on participating in all subsequent competitions, or only the next competition? Should a default result in a disadvantage instead of an outright ban? Should these determinations be made when future programs that will ( printed page 75487) make new covered funding awards are noticed?
The RBPA requires the Commission to “set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation” and stipulates that it “may not limit the base forfeiture to an amount less than 30 percent of the applicant's total support, unless the Commission demonstrates the need for lower penalties in a particular instance.” The Commission believes this RBPA provision addresses defaults after an applicant becomes a winning bidder or is selected by the Commission to receive support, but before it is authorized to receive funding.
Regarding pre-authorization defaults, a winning bidder that fails to file an application by the applicable deadline or that for any reason is not subsequently authorized to receive support has defaulted on its bid. The Commission may dismiss a winning bidder's application with prejudice for failure of the winning bidder to prosecute, failure of the winning bidder to respond substantially within the time period specified in official correspondence or requests for additional information, or failure of the winning bidder to comply with requirements for becoming authorized to receive support. Any such determination by the Bureau shall be final upon public notice of the determination, and a winning bidder or long-form applicant shall have no opportunity to cure through additional submissions, negotiations, or otherwise. The Commission invites comment on retaining these definitions from 47 CFR 1.21004 and Auction 904.
The advent of the Commission's Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric opened new possibilities for defining service areas under new awards of covered funding. The Commission proposes to defer defining “violation” for the purposes of the RBPA until it adopts rules for specific high-cost mechanisms and identifies the geographic areas eligible for support. The Commission invites comment on the proposal.
Auction 904 limited the total base forfeiture to 15% of “the bidder's total assigned support for the Census Block Groups in which it is defaulting” to prevent the base forfeiture amount from being disproportionate to the amount of a winning bidder's bid. In light of Congress's desire to increase penalties for pre-authorization defaults, the Commission invites comment on defining “applicant's total support” as the entire amount of support won at auction, which could potentially increase penalties considerably. The Commission also invites proposals for alternative definitions, such as defining applicant's total support as the total defaulted bid amount. The Commission further invites comment on which factors would demonstrate the need for lower penalties in a particular instance, per section 254(m)(3)(D) of the Communications Act.
In the Commission's experience developing subsidy programs to spur deployment of broadband-capable networks, the Commission recognizes that program design can impact outcomes. Therefore, the Commission invites proposals addressing the design of high-cost support mechanisms that would reduce pre-authorization defaults, possibly through deterring potential applicants that are unlikely to meet program requirements if they receive support. The proposals could include limits on the number of locations an applicant can win relative to the number of locations that it currently serves or the applicant's current revenues—especially applicants that lack any current ETC designation or have not provided a voice, broadband, and/or electric transmission or distribution service for at least two years (or are not a wholly-owned subsidiary of such an entity). Commenters should address potential downsides of design proposals, including potentially hindering competition and rapidly exhausting program budgets. Proposals may also include solutions for expeditiously awarding support for locations that still need service after a winning bidder defaults, and specific penalties for post-authorization defaults when the Commission reasonably believes that the winning bidder did not intend to meet program requirements or otherwise acted in bad faith.

As required by the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980, as amended (RFA), the Commission has prepared the Initial Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (IRFA) of the policies and rules proposed in the NPRM assessing the possible significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities. The Commission requests written public comments on this IRFA. Comments must be identified as responses to the IRFA and must be filed by the deadlines for comments specified in this document. In addition, the NPRM and IRFA (or summaries thereof) will be published in the Federal Register .
The NPRM seeks comment on proposals for implementing the RBPA, which directs the Commission to initiate a rulemaking proceeding to establish a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, a new covered funding award. The NPRM also seeks comment on proposals for implementing the RBPA's penalties for pre-authorization defaults.
Specifically, the NPRM seeks comment on adopting a rule that would require future high-cost support mechanisms that will make new covered funding awards to include a vetting framework that requires proposals from applicants for funding to contain sufficient detail and documentation for the Commission to ascertain that the applicant possesses the technical, financial, and operational capabilities, and has a reasonable business plan, to deploy the proposed network and deliver services with the relevant performance characteristics and requirements defined by the Commission and as pledged by the applicant. The NPRM also seeks comment on the effectiveness of vetting frameworks used for prior high-cost support competitive bidding mechanisms but allows the details of the vetting framework to be determined when programs for new covered funding awards are noticed in the future.
The RFA directs agencies to provide a description of and, where feasible, an estimate of the number of small entities that may be affected by the proposed rules, if adopted. The RFA generally defines the term “small entity” as having the same meaning as the terms “small business,” “small organization,” and “small governmental jurisdiction.” In addition, the term “small business” has the same meaning as the term ( printed page 75488) “small business concern” under the Small Business Act. A “small business concern” is one which: (1) is independently owned and operated; (2) is not dominant in its field of operation; and (3) satisfies any additional criteria established by the Small Business Administration (SBA). The SBA establishes small business size standards that agencies are required to use when promulgating regulations relating to small businesses; agencies may establish alternative size standards for use in such programs, but must consult and obtain approval from SBA before doing so.
Commission actions, over time, may affect small entities that are not easily categorized at present. The Commission therefore describes three broad groups of small entities that could be directly affected by its actions. In general, a small business is an independent business having fewer than 500 employees. These types of small businesses represent 99.9% of all businesses in the United States, which translates to 34.75 million businesses. Next, “small organizations” are not-for-profit enterprises that are independently owned and operated and not dominant their field. While the Commission does not have data regarding the number of non-profits that meet that criteria, over 99 percent of nonprofits have fewer than 500 employees. Finally, “small governmental jurisdictions” are defined as cities, counties, towns, townships, villages, school districts, or special districts with populations of less than fifty thousand. Based on the 2022 U.S. Census of Governments data, the Commission estimates that at least 48,724 out of 90,835 local government jurisdictions have a population of less than 50,000.

The RFA directs agencies to describe the economic impact of proposed rules on small entities, as well as projected reporting, recordkeeping and other compliance requirements, including an estimate of the classes of small entities which will be subject to the requirements and the type of professional skills necessary for preparation of the report or record.
In the NPRM, the Commission seeks comment on proposals that, if adopted, would require future high-cost support program applicants, including small entities, to demonstrate that they possess the technical, financial, and operational capabilities to deploy the proposed network and deliver services with the relevant performance characteristics and requirements defined by the Commission. This includes proposed definitions for “covered funding” and the use of a two-stage application process for competitive bidding for high-cost support. Specifically, the NPRM seeks comment on the effectiveness of vetting frameworks used for prior high-cost support competitive bidding mechanisms while allowing the details of the vetting framework to be determined when programs for new covered funding awards are noticed in the future. The NPRM also seeks comment on proposals for implementing the RBPA's penalties for pre-authorization defaults.
The proposals in the NPRM would require that future high-cost support mechanisms that will make new covered funding awards include a vetting framework that complies with the RBPA, allowing the specifics of the framework to be detailed when the future high-cost mechanisms are noticed. This will allow the Commission to adopt a vetting framework that satisfies the RBPA and also comports with the specifics of a future mechanism that has not yet been proposed. Given that the proposed rules will not adopt the specific vetting framework to be used for future ( printed page 75489) programs, the Commission is uncertain of the impact on small entities at this time. However, small carriers that have participated in competitive bidding for high-cost support should be familiar with what is normally required of applicants for proving capabilities, such as audited financial statements, letters of credit, and ETC designation. The same measures have been used consistently across several mechanisms of competitive bidding for high-cost support and will likely be used in the future, perhaps with changes to the timing of the required submission during the competition. Under the RBPA, carriers will have greater certainty regarding the penalties for pre-authorization defaults on new covered funding awards. The proposed rules will only apply to future high-cost support mechanisms that make new covered funding awards. The Commission's previous competitive bidding programs for high-cost support attracted a broad array of applicants, including small entities. Before reaching its final conclusions and taking action in this proceeding, the Commission expects to review the comments filed in response to the NPRM, including costs and benefits of these proposed rules, and more fully consider the economic impact on small entities and how any impact can be minimized.
The RFA directs agencies to provide a description of any significant alternatives to the proposed rules that would accomplish the stated objectives of applicable statutes, and minimize any significant economic impact on small entities. The discussion is required to include alternatives such as: “(1) the establishment of differing compliance or reporting requirements or timetables that take into account the resources available to small entities; (2) the clarification, consolidation, or simplification of compliance and reporting requirements under the rule for such small entities; (3) the use of performance rather than design standards; and (4) an exemption from coverage of the rule, or any part thereof, for such small entities.”
In the NPRM, the Commission proposes new rules that may impact small entities and seeks comment on alternatives that may minimize any significant economic impact on small providers. Specifically, the Commission invites comment on alternative approaches for vetting applicants for future, new covered funding awards. This includes whether to request additional information, such as a business plan, with their application. The NPRM also seeks comment on whether small and other applicants that previously defaulted in a universal service program should be eligible to compete in new covered funding awards, and whether a history of compliance with other state and Federal programs should be included with the application. Alternative proposals and approaches from commenters will further develop the record and could help the Commission further minimize the economic impact on small entities. The Commission's evaluation of the comments filed in this proceeding will shape the final conclusions it reaches, the final alternatives it considers, and the actions it ultimately takes to minimize any possible economic impact the final rules may have on small entities.
Accordingly, it is ordered that pursuant to sections 1, 2, 4(i)-(j), 201(b), 254, 303(r), and 403 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, 47 U.S.C. 151, 152, 154(i)-(j), 201(b), 254, 303(r), and 403, and §§ 1.1 and 1.412 of the Commission's rules, 47 CFR 1.1, 1.412, the NPRM hereby is adopted.
It is further ordered that, pursuant to applicable procedures set forth in §§ 1.415 and 1.419 of the Commission's rules, 47 CFR 1.415, 1.419, interested parties may file comments on or before December 23, 2026, and reply comments on or before January 22, 2027.

2. Add § 54.323 to subpart D to read as follows:
Application process for new covered funding awards under the Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025.
(a) New Covered Funding Award. For purposes of this section, a New Covered Funding Award is an award of covered funding that is made based on an application submitted to the Commission on or after [ the date on which the Commission promulgates rules pursuant to the Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025]. Covered Funding means any new offer of high-cost universal service program funding with rules adopted after [ the date on which rules are promulgated pursuant to the Rural Broadband Protection Act of 2025], including funding provided through a reverse competitive bidding mechanism, for the deployment of a broadband-capable network and the provision of supported services over the network.
(b) Proceedings to adopt the mechanism-specific requirements for future high-cost support programs for distributing New Covered Funding Awards must propose, seek comment on, and adopt a vetting process for applicants for, and other recipients of, the new covered funding award under the specific high-cost support mechanism at issue.
(c) The vetting process developed under paragraph (b) of this section must, at a minimum, require an applicant for a new covered funding award to include in its initial application a proposal containing sufficient detail and documentation for the Commission to ascertain that the applicant possesses the technical, financial, and operational capabilities, and has a reasonable business plan, to deploy the proposed network and deliver services with the relevant performance characteristics and requirements defined by the Commission and as certified by the applicant.
(d) The Commission shall evaluate the applicant proposal described in paragraph (c) of this section against reasonable and well-established technical, financial, and operational standards, including the technical standards adopted by the Commission in orders of the Commission relating to Establishing the Digital Opportunity Data Collection (WC Docket No. 19-195) (or orders of the Commission relating to modernizing any successor collection) for purposes of entities that must report broadband availability coverage and the applicant's history of complying with requirements in Commission and other government broadband deployment funding programs.
(e) In adopting rules for any new covered funding award, the Commission ( printed page 75490) shall set a penalty for pre-authorization defaults of at least $9,000 per violation and may not limit the base forfeiture to an amount less than 30 percent of the applicant's total support, unless the Commission demonstrates the need for lower penalties in a particular instance.

summary: Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser. What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex
content:
Fundraiser by Heather Liu : Help A #MeToo Survivor and Daughter Win Their Case
Heather Liu is organizing this fundraiser.
What I’ve experienced isn’t what any woman should ever go through. First there was the violence of non-consensual sex forced on me, followed by lies and denial. Then, rare moments of hope, followed by setbacks tinged with revenge from a father whose fear of revealing truth drives him to deny his child’s existence. This child is my daughter. For 20 years I’ve hidden the nightmare involving her origin by my silence, partly due to the sense of shame and partly because the father of my child is a influential public figure. Till the rapist has pushed us to a corner by threatening our existence with vicious conspiracy theories.
（我經歷了任何一位女性都不該經歷的事情。先是遭遇性侵，接著還要面對謊言、抵賴和詆毀。過去20年來，間或閃現的希望，卻因我女兒的生父拒絕承認這孩子的存在，而淹沒在長久的幻滅中。過去20年來，我一直對女兒的身世三緘其口，讓一段揮之不去的夢魘深藏內心，一方面出於羞辱感，另一方面無法面對孩子的生父作為一個公眾人物給我心靈帶來的扭曲。）
With your help, the truth of our experience will be told. When it is, I hope justice will prevail. This is why I’m emerging from the shadows.
（因您伸出援手，我將得以說出這段真實的經歷。當真相大白的那一天到來，我希望正義能夠隨之彰顯。）
In 2000, I was a journalist working for a local Chinese newspaper in Los Angeles. I was assigned to interview a famous Chinese dissident, a political refugee in America, who people called the “Godfather of the Democratic Movement in China.” I wrote the story, but in doing so, my life was changed forever by his sexual assault of me.
（2000年，身為洛杉磯當地一家中文媒體記者的我，被派去採訪一位著名的中國異議人士，也是我本人非常敬仰的政治流亡者、一位被視為「中國民主運動之父」的風雲人物。我完成了採訪任務，然而我的個人生活卻因今生與他這唯一的遭逢而徹底脫軌。）
Let’s just say, nine months after I did that story, I gave birth to my daughter, who bore no resemblance to my then-husband. My husband knew why since I’d told him about the sexual assault after it happened. My marriage ended, and my life as a single mom began. To protect my daughter and me from possible backlash about how she was conceived and her father’s identity, I kept my ordeal quiet. The two of us moved to Hong Kong.
（在我做了那次採訪的9個月之後，我的女兒降生了。她跟我當時的丈夫長得一點也不像，而我丈夫也並不感到驚訝，因為我早跟他坦白了我遭遇性侵的事。我的婚姻其實從那時起已名存實亡，我作為一個單親母親的生涯也即將開始。為了遠離各種因孩子身世而產生的猜忌，讓我和孩子可以過安靜而屬於自己的生活，同時也為了可以就近得到父母家人的幫忙照顧，我帶著孩子離開了美國，赴香港尋找發展機會。）
Through the years I never thought about contacting my daughter's biological father, whom I met only once. I didn’t consider doing this even after I lost my job as an editor in 2012. But then a former colleague, Beifeng, left Hong Kong for the United States. He’d criticized me for "depriving the child the right to be recognized by her father," and later persuaded me to let him bring a lock of my daughter’s hair, wrapped it in tissue paper, that he took with him to the United States.
（多年來，我從未想過要聯絡孩子的生父，那個我只見過一面的人，哪怕是2012年我失業的時候也沒萌生這個打算。我根本已經忘記了這個人，要不是當時正要動身赴美的前同事北風（我告訴了他我的孩子生父是誰，但沒有讓他知道詳情，他也沒有探問）批評我「剝奪孩子認父的權利」。他太太當即揪了孩子幾根頭髮，用手紙包了起來。）
Months later, my heart sank when Beifeng reported back to me that this man had denied everything, even the possibility of knowing me, let alone the possibility of having fathered a child. He’d committed this horrible crime against me, but he refused to acknowledge this truth. For to accept that he’d fathered a daughter, he’d have to admit how she came to existence. It appeared that he was refusing to allow his carefully crafted story about his “heroic” life to be marred by acknowledging his daughter’s existence.
（幾個月之後，北風帶來消息並深表意外地說，孩子的生父得知自己可能有個孩子時的反應，竟是敷衍和閃躲，好像根本不可能有這回事一樣。他當然寧肯忘記自己做過的事，但真相怎麼能因你不想面對就可以不承認、孩子怎麼可以就這樣當她不存在呢？就像他後來在郵件裡提到的，他所關切的，是這事將來在他的回憶錄裡該怎麼寫，而不是他身為人父應該盡什麼責。他在意的只是他自己英雄般的人生，無論如何不能留下任何污點。）
After this news reached me, I was diagnosed with clinical depression and started to see a doctor regularly. Professionally, however, I had to appear calm and collected so I could earn a living that would support the two of us. I worked as a freelance writer and translator, while also raising my daughter on my own.
（我聞訊心裡沉了一下，不久開始意識恍惚，甚至試過下班下車記不起回家的方向。我遠在北京的母親聽說之後，在電話的另一頭啜泣得聲音哽咽。2013年2月，我被確診患上抑鬱症。失業更兼病倒，令我們母女的生計雪上加霜，這期間我成為自由撰稿人，還要硬撐著努力譯書維持生計。好在偶爾有父母幫手、妹妹接濟一下，才度過了一段危機。）
Five years later, in 2018, in the midst of #MeToo movement, when sexual abuse and harassment were receiving public attention globally, rumors spread online about this famous Chinese man having fathered an illegitimate child. At that point, I contacted him by phone from Hong Kong and boldly asked for child support.
（一晃又過了5年，時間到了2018年，在#MeToo（「我也是受害者」）運動的聲浪中，性侵和性騷擾現象的普遍存在引起了全球性輿論關注。在此期間，網上首次出現了對我女兒的生父「不認親」的議論。已變得反應遲緩的我這才開始應對，邁出了主動聯繫孩子生父這一步。）
He agreed to a DNA test that was performed privately in Washington D.C.., The DNA results proved that he was Charlotte's father. The person who shared the results with him said that he had responded positively to having a daughter. Accordingly, when I contacted him again, he promised to assist us by at least paying for her education. But later on, since I would not change my tone on the unhappy encounter with him in the past, he decided to deny being Charlotte’s father and began to challenge the DNA results, shirked his responsibility as her biological father, and ignored that I was a victim of his violent sexual assault.
（他於是主動提出做個DNA鑑定，並指定了一位背景相當可靠的前白宮幕僚做中間人，在華盛頓特區進行了DNA樣本的收集與鑑定。結果出來後，中間人率先通知我，說結果證明魏先生是孩子的生父無疑，並告訴我，魏先生對鑑定結果表示認可並顯得「很開心」。據此，在我與孩子的生父再次聯繫時，他表示自己起碼會負擔孩子的大學學費。但真到了時候他又變卦了，甚至仗著沒有把DNA鑑定結果如約給我們，便想將已經做過DNA鑑定這事也想賴掉。）
The rest of the story is detailed in Huaizhao Liu v. Jingsheng Wei, case #1:19-cv-03344, which was heard in the Washington, D.C. federal court. Charlotte’s father managed to find the funds necessary to hire a high-powered defense attorney to help him to deny both our dignity and his basic obligations of paternity.
（後來的事情見華盛頓特區聯邦法院卷宗（Case Number 1:19-cv-03344）。我女兒的生父大手筆聘請了專攻白領犯罪辯護的名牌大狀為自己的辯護律師，竭力搬弄法律條文進行技術性規避，想就此永遠掩蓋真相，踐踏我們母女的權益與尊嚴。）
We believe that Charlotte’s biological father should be forced to keep his promise of supporting her education, and we are asking that he release the DNA test results to us. His 19-year old daughter deserves to know the truth.
（我們堅信，法庭應該為這位竭力否認已經做過親子鑑定的生父驗明正身，然後強制他履行他的諾言，承擔他女兒的學費。我們堅信，他19歲的女兒有權利知曉真相。）
The weight of evidence is on our side, but we risk losing the lawsuit that we are filing against him if we cannot raise the money we need to hire an attorney who is as capable as his lawyer. What is at risk is Charlotte's right to a quality education, along with the legally binding acknowledgement of his paternity.
（儘管我們掌握活生生的證據，但如果籌不到聘請律師的費用，單憑我們自訴，將無法應對複雜的陪審團庭審程序。立案至今一年多來，被告採取躲和拖的戰術，先是躲傳票，然後提出「司法管轄權」爭議逼我們撤案，一計不成又援引「多國籍」條款，將案子從特區高等法院轉移到聯邦法院。）
With your assistance – with your contributions – we intend to hire an attorney who is experienced in sexual assault and paternity cases. We hope to win this #MeToo case and pursue respectful, equal and democratic human relationship in Chinese community.
（您的捐助將幫助我們聘請到專攻性侵案和親子案官司的律師，幫我們贏得這場事關尊嚴、平等、人權以及人性的人身傷害官司，並藉此推動美國的華人社區乃至全球華人的觀念進步與行為的現代化。）
Here are some online stories and commentary about this, in Chinese:
https://www.storm.mg/article/2891777?mode=whole
(by Liao Yiwu, award winner of Human Rights Watch Hellman-Hammett Grant 2003, the German Geschwister-Scholl-Preis 2011 and the Peace Prize of the German Book Trade 2012.)
（作者/廖亦武，詩人、流亡作家與底層歷史記錄者。2012年德國書業和平獎得主，並曾獲美國《當代基督教》雜誌頒發的「最佳圖書奬」、德國書業協會頒發的「紹爾兄妹獎」、德國廣播協會頒發的「最佳廣播劇奬」及德國阿夏芬堡頒發的「公民勇氣奬」。2013年，法國政府頒發給廖亦武「法蘭西文學藝術軍官獎章」。2018年，廖亦武獲美國紐約瓦茨拉夫 哈維爾圖書基金會頒發「無懼危難作家獎」。）
http://minzhuzhongguo.org/MainArtShow.aspx?AID=105641
(by Qi JIazhen, writer in exile, author of autobiographical series: Tears of the Goddess of Liberty and Red Dog. Qi is the Chairwoman of the Women Writers committee, Independent Chinese PEN Center.)
（作者/齊家貞，流亡作家，著有系列傳記《自由神的眼泪──父女两代囚徒的真實故事》（後改名《黑牆裡的倖存者》和《紅狗：—個被釋女囚的真實故事》在香港和台灣出版。齊家貞曾先後擔任國際筆會獨立中文筆會理事會理事、副會長、秘書長等職務，並在澳洲建立了“齊氏文化基金會”，每年頒發“推動中國進步獎”截至2019年已連續頒獎12屆。）
https://liuvswei.blogspot.com/2020/08/metoo.html
(by Lau Kayee, Chairwoman of Network for Women In Politics, Hong Kong; Spokeswoman of Hong Kong Civil Human Rights Front.)
（作者/劉家儀，香港婦女參政網絡主席，六四新生代秘書長，支聯會常委，香港市民捍衛人權陣線發言人。）
With your contributions, we will be able to set a positive example for #MeToo victims by raising awareness about women’s and children's rights, globally.
因您的資助，我們將能夠為#MeToo運動傷害者們建立一個積極的個案，為提高女性及孩童的權利意識而有所貢獻。

content:
Fundraiser by Boston Standswithhk : US Hong Kong Safe Harbor Postcard Campaign
Boston Standswithhk is organizing this fundraiser.
***When donation, make as anonymous if you wish to hide the donator's name and make the TIPS to 0.00***
While US-China tensions continue to escalate and the November presidential elections loom near, as Hongkongers living in the United States (or any informed person in the world), we must not forget or turn a blind eye to the CCP’s continuous oppression on Hongkongers and other minority groups in China, such as Uyghurs, Tibetans, and Mongolians. With the promulgation of the new National Security Law on June 30, 2020, the government has since been arresting and charging dissidents with these vaguely-worded laws that may entail life imprisonment. In the past month alone, 12 Hong Kongers fleeing protest-related charges have been detained in China and denied meetings with lawyers since August 23, 2020; Legislative Council elections had been postponed a year in the name of “public health concerns” amidst a mass arrest of candidates; media mogul Jimmy Lai, who runs the only pro-democratic print newspaper in Hong Kong, has been arrested with the National Security Law; and the Education Bureau has begun actively censoring content they deemed politically incorrect in Liberal Studies textbooks, including concepts like “civil disobedience” and “separation of powers”, and images of Lennon Walls. Up until today, the administration has arrested more than 10,000 Hong Kongers, charged over 2,200, deployed water cannons, fired more than 16,000 tear gas canisters and over 10,000 rubber bullets against its own people. Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and political rights as we knew it have been thoroughly eroded.
11月的美國總統大選逐漸逼近，中美關係日漸緊張，作為居住在美國的香港人或是在這個世界上任何有良知的人，面對中共對香港、維吾爾族、藏族和蒙古族的持續壓逼，我們不能容忍，更不能視而不見。自2020年6月30日頒布《國家安全法》以來，政府持續逮捕異見人​​士，並以措辭含糊的法律起訴抗爭者，香港的司法制度已經徹底淪為政府的打壓工具。及後更有12名香港抗爭者為了逃離這種不公義的審判欲流亡台灣，卻被中共非法拘捕。他們無法與律師會面，音訊全無。而香港人僅有的發聲方法——立法會選舉，卻因為「公共衛生風險」而被推遲一年；同時間，大批候選人被逮捕或是被拒絕參選。作為香港唯一異見紙媒《蘋果日報》的老闆黎智英被警方高調逮捕，《蘋果日報》總部更被大肆搜查。教育局亦積極審查通識科教科書中所謂的「政治不正確」內容，例如「公民抗命」和「三權分立」的概念，以及連儂牆相片。到今天為止，已經有超過10,000多名香港人被捕、2,200多人被起訴，警方向市民發射了超過16,000枚催淚彈和10,000多發橡皮子彈，令香港人長期生活在恐懼中。香港人的言論自由、集會自由和政治權利已被徹底侵蝕。
In light of the deteriorating situation, we plan to kickstart a new round of postcard campaign urging Congress to pass two bills related to Hong Kong as soon as possible - Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act (H.R.7415/S.4110), and Hong Kong People’s Freedom and Choice Act (H.R.7428/S.4229):
鑑於情況日益惡化，我們希望透過郵寄明信片給國會議員的方式，呼籲他們盡快通過兩項與香港有關的法案 —— 香港安全港法案 (H.R.7415 / S.4110) 和香港人民自由與選擇法(H.R.7428 / S.4229):
The Hong Kong Safe Harbor Act will designate certain Hong Kong residents who are victims of persecution or who have a well-founded fear of future persecution because of their peaceful political activities as Priority 2 refugees (excluded from refugee cap), allowing them and their spouses, children, parents to apply to the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for protection. (Click here for more details)
《香港安全港法案》將指定某些遭受迫害，或因其參與和平的政治活動而感到恐懼的香港居民列為「優先級別2」的難民，且不受每年限額限制，亦允許他們及其配偶、子女、父母向「美國難民接納計劃」申請庇護。(詳情請瀏覽)
The Hong Kong People's Freedom and Choice Act will provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Hong Kongers, maintain Hong Kong’s status as autonomous for the purposes of immigration, provide special and expedited status for certain high-skilled Hong Kongers as well as expedite Permanent Resident status for Hong Kongers residing in the US. (Click here for more details)
《香港人民自由與選擇法》會為香港人提供臨時保護身份（TPS），維持香港在移民方面的自治地位，亦為部分香港專業人仕提供特殊和快速的身份，並加快辦理香港人的美國永久居民(綠卡)身份的程序。(詳情請瀏覽)
In our last postcard campaign pushing for the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act, we delivered over 3000 postcards to Congress. We aren’t part of any formal organization and do not have operation funds. We desperately call for your contribution again to help us deliver these postcards to Congress, to remind them of Hong Kong’s urgent situation and urge them to take immediate action. Your contribution would support our printing and delivery costs. Thank you so much!
在上一次推動《香港人權與民主法》的明信片運動中，我們向國會送出了超過3000張的明信片。我們不是任何正式組織的成員，也沒有運營資金，所以我們竭誠呼籲您為我們提供資金，並幫助我們將這些明信片送交您們所屬的國會議員，提醒他們香港的緊急狀況，並呼籲他們立即採取行動。所有受到的捐款將支持我們的打印和交付成本。萬分感謝！

10月31日，台北市市长蒋万安（左）与民进党市长候选人沉普马在台北举行的首次电视辩论前合影。中央通讯社资料图（仅供参考）
中新社台北11月21日电 国民党台北市市长蒋万安与民进党市长候选人沉伯洋周六因幼稚园虐童案、食物中毒事件、水库安装太阳能电池板计划等儿童福利和公共卫生问题发生冲突。
沉在11月28日大选前的第二场电视政策演讲中发表讲话，指责国民党领导的台北市政府对危机反应太慢，并列举了查里斯幼儿园虐待事件、2024年造成六人死亡的Polam咖啡店食物中毒事件以及附近建筑造成的大直社区建筑物倒塌事件。
沉说，市政府1999年通过热线电话收到了13起有关查里斯的投诉，但未能妥善调查这些投诉。
在 Polam Kopitiam 事件中，官员在接到报告五小时后赶到，但未能立即保存可疑食品，沉说，这导致了另外 8 起食物中毒案件。
监察院后来谴责该市未能采取应有的谨慎态度。
沉说：“如果我成为市长，在涉及儿童安全的问题上，我宁愿过多干预，也不愿迟到。”他承诺，一旦虐待指控得到证实，将立即暂停儿童保育人员的工作并关闭设施。
周六，民进党台北市长候选人沉彪马在与蒋介石的第二次电视政策演讲后向媒体致意。中央通讯社照片2026年11月21日
与此同时，蒋介石重申反对在台北主要饮用水源翡翠水库安装太阳能电池板，并表示中央政府已三度致函台北市，要求其评估潜在的安装地点并解释其反对意见。
这个问题已成为一场竞选争议，国民党对民进党统治城市的两个水库漂浮的太阳能电池板潜在的健康风险表示担忧，民进党则以政府在这些水库进行的水测试为由指责其散布谣言。
蒋说：“保护我们的水源不仅仅是口号。我已经采取实际行动来维护大台北地区600万人民获得清洁饮用水的权利。”
他还呼吁中央政府在幼儿园强制安装监控摄像头，并指出台北自2024年起对私立幼儿园安装监控摄像头提供全额补贴，并要求录像至少保留90天。
蒋介石提出了以四大走廊为中心的20年发展计划，其中人工智能（AI）是关键的经济驱动力。
他重点介绍了连接北投士林科技园、内湖科技园和南港软件园的北部科技走廊，并引用了英伟达公司决定进驻北投士林园区的决定。
他表示，他的政府已帮助推动了 421 个重大投资项目，价值超过 1038 亿新台币（31.4 亿美元），其中包括 223 个人工智能相关项目。

Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang, Shen debate child, food, water safety - Focus Taiwan
2026 ELECTIONS/Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang, Shen debate child, food, water safety

Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (left) and DPP mayoral candidate Puma Shen pose together before their first televised debate in Taipei on Oct. 31. CNA file photo for illustrative purposes
Taipei, Nov. 21 (CNA) Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) of the Kuomintang (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋) clashed Saturday over the handling of child welfare and public health issues, including a child abuse case at a kindergarten, a deadly food poisoning incident and plans to install solar panels at a reservoir.
Speaking at the second televised policy presentation ahead of the Nov. 28 election, Shen accused the KMT-led Taipei City government of responding too slowly to crises, citing the abuse case at Charisse Kindergarten, the Polam Kopitiam food poisoning incident that killed six people in 2024, and the collapse of buildings in the Dazhi neighborhood caused by nearby construction.
Shen said the city government received 13 complaints about Charisse through its 1999 hotline but failed to properly investigate the complaints.
In the Polam Kopitiam case, officials arrived five hours after receiving a report and failed to immediately preserve suspected food items, which Shen said led to eight additional cases of food poisoning.
The Control Yuan later censured the city over its failure to exercise due care.
"If I become mayor, when it comes to children's safety, I would rather intervene too much than be late," Shen said, pledging to immediately suspend childcare workers and shut down facilities when abuse allegations were substantiated.
DPP Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen greets the press on Saturday after his and Chiang's second televised policy presentation. CNA photo Nov. 21, 2026
Chiang, meanwhile, reiterated his opposition to installing solar panels at Feitsui Reservoir, Taipei's main source of drinking water, saying the central government had written to the city three times asking it to assess potential installation sites and explain its objections.
The issue has become a campaign controversy, with the KMT raising concerns about potential health risks from floating solar panels at two reservoirs located in DPP-governed cities and the DPP accusing it of spreading rumors, citing government water tests at those reservoirs.
"Protecting our water sources takes more than slogans. I have taken concrete action to safeguard the right of 6 million people in greater Taipei to clean drinking water," Chiang said.
He also called on the central government to make surveillance cameras mandatory in kindergartens, noting that Taipei has fully subsidized their installation at private kindergartens since 2024, requiring footage to be retained for at least 90 days.
Chiang proposed a 20-year development plan centered on four corridors, with artificial intelligence (AI) serving as a key economic driver.
He highlighted the northern technology corridor linking Beitou-Shilin Technology Park, Neihu Technology Park and Nangang Software Park, citing Nvidia Corp.'s decision to establish a presence in the Beitou-Shilin park.
He said his administration had helped facilitate 421 major investment projects worth more than NT$103.8 billion (US$3.14 billion), including 223 AI-related projects worth over NT$66.3 billion.
Chiang also pledged to expand AI research and computing resources, establish an AI startup fund and develop Beitou-Shilin Technology Park into a pilot area for smart transportation technologies featuring autonomous buses and intelligent traffic systems.
Opposition KMT's incumbent Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (center) speaks to the press on Saturday after his and Shen's second televised policy presentation. CNA photo Nov. 21, 2026
Other priorities included planting another 40,000 trees, developing underground drainage facilities to address extreme rainfall, expanding public transportation and building additional sports centers and cultural facilities.
Shen, meanwhile, pledged to publish a checklist of his campaign promises against which residents could assess his performance, saying residents would judge his performance.
He also promised closer cooperation with frontline civil servants, saying mayors should take responsibility for policy decisions rather than leave subordinates to deal with the fallout from policy decisions.
Citing Chiang's proposals to relocate Songshan Airport and establish a smoke-free city, Shen said policies should not be announced without consulting city departments and assessing implementation risks.
He also proposed establishing a Taipei policy research institute to support civil servants and ensure frontline workers, including social workers and teachers, were not left to face public criticism alone when problems arose.

Posted Fri 20 Nov 2026 at 2:21pmFri 20 Nov 2026 at 2:21pmFri 20 Nov 2026 at 2:21pm
中国高度评价这次“和平峰会”，称其意义重大，影响深远，“是载入史册的标志性事件”。 (Win McNamee/Pool via Reuters)
中国国家主席习近平、美国总统特朗普与俄罗斯总统普京在深圳APEC峰会期间举行历史性的三方会晤。会谈进行了约90分钟，随后发表了一份仅有五段话的《中俄美元首和平宣言》。
宣言重申“核战争打不赢也打不得”，并表示三国将就“减少核风险、防止核扩散进行对话”，但没有给出时间表。特朗普自第一任期以来一直力推的三边核裁军谈判，宣言只字未提。宣言同样没有提及俄乌战争，也没有提及美国与伊朗的冲突。
中国外长王毅在峰会后的记者会上高度评价这是一次“和平峰会”，意义重大，影响深远，“是载入史册的标志性事件”，向世界发出了积极信号。
会晤结束后，各方反应也迅速而分化。特朗普称会谈“大获成功”。普京一边炫耀外交收获，一边就克里米亚大桥再度遇袭发出强硬警告。欧洲盟友则忙于切割“雅尔塔”式的联想。
习近平主持三方峰会。 (Sputnik: Vyacheslav Prokofyev via Reuters)
在会谈开场白中，特朗普对习近平和普京说：“我们正在创造历史。”他还说：“从来没有哪种和平是靠拒绝接触的机会换来的。”
会后，他在返回华盛顿的专机上接受了多家媒体采访，基调是自我肯定。
他对美国全国广播公司（NBC）说，会谈“进行得很好”，并给自己打分：“如果满分是10分，我觉得是12分。建立了了不起的关系。”
被问及称普京为“我的朋友”是否合适，特朗普为自己辩护：“有拥有4000枚核武器的人做朋友，总比做敌人好。”他同时称习近平为朋友和“了不起的领导人”。
核军控是特朗普此行的重点目标之一，但他承认难度很大。
他对路透社说：“我喜欢这个构想，但就纯粹的谈判而言，对我这个总统来说非常困难。”
他说习近平在“构想”上与他看法一致，“但与此同时，让一个人说‘我们有4000枚核武器，我们削减一半’，是很难做到的”。他表示会继续提这件事，“因为这件事应该做，但在心理上很难做到”。
特朗普在参加三方峰会之前与习近平举行了双边会晤。 (Mark Schiefelbein/Pool via Reuters)
在伊朗问题上，他似乎把是否再度发动大规模打击的决定推迟到明年，说：“年初之后，我再跟你们谈这个。”他还补充说：“我们有时间。”
特朗普还表示，这次在深圳没能与金正恩会面，因为“会议太多了”，但两人“会在某个时候”见面。
蒙纳士大学商学院教授史鹤凌接受ABC中文采访说，这次峰会在经济方面“不大可能产生一些实质性的推动”。
他说，从中国角度来讲，希望是美国降低关税，因为中国现在整个经济基本上是靠出口的支撑。
“美国根本不可能大规模的来降低点关税，”他说，“可能唯一能够达成一些协议的就是地区安全方面的。”
普京称特朗普总统似乎真心致力于结束乌克兰战争。 (Reuters: Maxim Shemetov/Pool)
普京在昨晚离开深圳前举行了记者会，表示他与中美两国领导人举行了一次“坦率而有益的”会晤，并称特朗普总统似乎真心致力于结束乌克兰战争，俄美关系有可能改善，特朗普政府对莫斯科的态度令人有理由保持乐观。
他说三国“在解决地区冲突方面有许多共同利益，显然也包括乌克兰冲突”。他表示“和平宣言”并没有设定宏大的目标，也不会强迫任何人遵守峰会的决定。
在核不扩散问题上，普京并没有展开阐述，只是简单提到三方会晤讨论了联合国改革、安全问题和核不扩散。
莫斯科把这次会晤包装成地缘政治上的胜利：既显示欧洲孤立俄罗斯的努力以失败告终，也显示俄罗斯在世界事务中举足轻重。
普京表示，俄方承认乌克兰有权享有自身安全，但不能以损害俄罗斯的安全为代价。
他说，欧盟正朝着成为军事政治集团的方向发展，对俄罗斯而言，这是一个挑战。俄罗斯不能接受乌克兰与欧盟之间任何形式的军事合作，包括欧盟可能向乌克兰部署军队。
对于外界把深圳会晤比作雅尔塔会议，普京反驳说：“我想强调这一点，希望说得一清二楚：雅尔塔并没有把世界划分为‘势力范围’。雅尔塔只是承认了二战之后出现的现实。他们还能怎么办？让战争继续下去吗？”
他还说：“雅尔塔只是把既有现实固定下来。在今天的冲突中，我们同样必须接受实地的现实。”这句“实地现实”是普京常用的说法，用来要求乌克兰接受俄方的和平条件，而基辅则认为这等于投降。
在欧洲能否参与和谈的问题上，普京说：“我们明白，讨论安全问题，包括欧洲的安全，没有欧洲人参与是毫无意义的。”
“我们不反对，但需要了解欧洲会带来什么。通过外交渠道，我们已提议欧洲代表来莫斯科，以便弄清他们的立场。之后，我们再决定以何种形式继续与乌克兰对话，”普京说。
就在中美俄深圳峰会前后，欧洲盟友在柏林召开“意愿联盟”会议，德国、法国、英国、波兰、意大利和北约领导人出席，美国特使威特科夫和库什纳也在场。
特朗普通过电话参加了会议。他对路透社说，自己传达的信息是：“普京总统想达成协议，他们想达成协议，每个人都想达成协议，那就达成协议吧。”
特朗普称普京为他的“朋友”。 (Reuters: Sputnik/Vyacheslav Prokofyev)
德、法、英、乌领导人在会后的联合声明中说，俄罗斯无法拖垮乌克兰主要盟友的坚定支持。据报道，英国首相伯纳姆称，美欧在乌克兰问题上数月来首次真正达成一致。
德国总理默茨则直接回应了“雅尔塔”的类比：“‘雅尔塔模式’不会带来和平。”
他表示各国领导人不会允许欧洲被瓜分，并把中美俄深圳峰会淡化为“一次拍照机会”。他也强调：“美国明白，没有我们就不可能有和平。反过来，我们也知道，有美国在我们身边，和平的前景会增加。”
波兰总理图斯克说：“普京先生不是我们的朋友，永远也不会是。”
丹麦首相弗雷泽里克森说，她觉得特朗普愿意与普京坐下来“非常难以理解”，并警告普京“在今天的会晤之后会更加有恃无恐。他看起来很高兴”。
北约秘书长吕特则表示，核大国领导人会面属正常现象，并称赞特朗普一直在为乌克兰和平付出“极其艰巨的努力”，“我只能表示赞赏”。
被记者问及特朗普称普京为“我的朋友”，乌克兰总统泽连斯基只是耸了耸肩，然后走开。
习近平、特朗普和普京在举行三方会晤前合影。 (Reuters: Win McNamee)
美国参议院民主党领袖查尔斯·舒默（Charles Schumer）的批评最为激烈。他称这场三方峰会是“一场将被人们长久铭记的历史性难堪”，并说：“这是对美国的背叛，出自一位最爱向对手鞠躬、只为拍照的总统。”
军控界的反应相对克制。美国军控协会执行主任达里尔·金博尔（Daryl Kimball）认为，重申核战争打不得是“积极”的，但他说：“我们需要的远不止言辞。我们需要在裁军外交上采取行动。”
伦敦皇家联合军种研究所（Royal United Services Institute）国际事务主任乔纳森·艾亚尔（Jonathan Eyal）接受路透社采访时表示，关注宣言中关于“国家官员享有豁免”以及“国际刑事法院以及其他类似机构不得滥用管辖权”。
国际刑事法院在三年多前就乌克兰境内的涉嫌战争罪行对普京及其他俄罗斯官员发出逮捕令。莫斯科否认这些指控。
艾亚尔认为宣言中“针对国际规范和法院的反弹是最有意思的一点”，并说：“大国发号施令，小国承受苦果。”
在他看来，普京是这场峰会的赢家，特朗普得到的则是一个“他并不需要的拍照机会”。
分析人士指出，特朗普此行是想在共和党于本月中期选举中失去国会控制权之后，提振自己的政治声望。
一个月后，特朗普将在其位于佛罗里达的高尔夫度假村主办二十国集团（G20）峰会，预计将再次会晤习近平，并可能与普京见面。
普京说，他与特朗普讨论过出席事宜，会考虑参加，但需要顾及俄国内的情况。
周四，在中美俄三方会晤开始前数小时，阿尔巴尼斯在APEC会议上利用发言时间点名普京。他说：“我非常直接地对普京总统说：结束你的战争，现在就结束。”
据报道，他说这番话时直视普京，但普京没有抬头。习近平和特朗普当时也在场。
阿尔巴尼斯警告，乌克兰和中东等地的冲突正在推高通胀，加重家庭预算压力，并表示欢迎三方会晤，希望取得“符合世界利益的积极成果”。
澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯与中国国家主席习近平在深圳举行双边会晤。 (Lintao Zhang/Pool via Reuters)
阿尔巴尼斯今天（11月20日）在深圳与习近平举行了双边会晤。
习近平说，在阿尔巴尼斯政府执政的过去四年里，中澳关系“尽管存在分歧”，仍实现了“全面转圜”。
他还说：“我愿同你本着平等、求同存异、互利合作的精神，推动中澳全面战略伙伴关系向前发展。”
阿尔巴尼斯说，澳中关系“为两国带来繁荣”，但承诺会进行“坦率”的交谈。
他说：“我们正在构建的关系是积极的、平静的，不以分歧来界定，而是可以为了共同利益进行清晰、坦率的交流。”
这是自阿尔巴尼斯2022年上台以来两人的第五次会晤。当时两国关系已跌至数十年来的最低点，北京对澳大利亚出口产品实施贸易限制，两国高层对话基本冻结。
阿尔巴尼斯随后赴北京与李强举行年度会谈，并出席中澳企业家圆桌会议。
必和必拓、力拓、澳新银行等澳大利亚大企业高管今天将在北京与中方同行会面，寻求更好的市场准入和公平竞争保证。
澳大利亚工商理事会（BCA）将推动中方进一步开放牛肉、大米等农产品市场，消除医疗科技企业面临的贸易壁垒，提高专业资格互认，并探讨人工智能和钢铁减排合作。
不过，阿尔巴尼斯访华前夕刚与菲律宾签署防务合作协议，参加了四方机制峰会，并签署了一项美国牵头的人工智能供应链协议，这些举动北京未必乐见。

從挑戰者轉變為尋求連任者，台北市長蔣萬安的選戰幕僚形容，蔣萬安沒變的是謀定而後動、務實勤懇的性格，盼用親和力贏得選民信任。圖為蔣萬安於115年10月8日宣布規劃松山機場遷建。中央社記者葉蓁芸攝 115年11月22日
（中央社記者葉蓁芸台北22日電）台北市長選舉熱戰，尋求連任的蔣萬安走入市場及宮廟，展現親和力。幕僚形容，蔣萬安個性溫柔，但領導、推動市政態度堅毅，帶領團隊往「對的方向」堅定前行，力拚勝選「光榮台北」。
蔣萬安畢業於建國中學、政治大學，曾赴美留學及工作，返台後於2016年投入北市第三選區（中山、松山）立委選舉當選，連任立委後在2022年參選台北市長，成為台北市升格直轄市後最年輕的民選市長。
由於蔣萬安父親蔣孝嚴曾任立法委員、外交部長，蔣萬安的從政之路註定備受各界關注。
蔣萬安被外界視為「根正苗藍」，過去在同性婚姻、性平議題展現的態度，被視為吸引年輕世代關鍵之一。蔣萬安接任市長後，從立委質詢台走向市長備詢台，市政表現受到媒體與議會的高度關注，個人談話風格、領導統御作風也成為討論話題。
身為同黨同志，國民黨台北市議長戴錫欽認為，蔣萬安個性溫和，不以強硬言詞反駁，偶爾針對特殊議題展現強悍態度，「但那終究不是常態」，蔣萬安多半選擇溫和態度回應外界質疑。
戴錫欽直言，蔣萬安許多政績普遍受到市民肯定，但在選舉過程中執行及危機處理出現瑕疵，因而被放大檢視，「有則改之、無則加勉」，盼不影響政策為市民帶來的正面影響。
蔣萬安投入選戰後，頻頻現身市場掃街、宮廟福宴等場合，展現親切態度與選民互動，彎下身緊握每一雙手，不漏掉任何人，面對支持者邀請合照、簽名也來者不拒，展現高度親和力。
前台北漁產運銷公司董事長鄭世維是蔣萬安選戰幕僚，陪蔣萬安走過4年前的選戰以及挑戰連任。他形容，比起上次的生澀，蔣萬安現在面對選民更接地氣，拜票扎實不馬虎，這次選戰激烈，蔣萬安放低身段，展現誠懇態度，民眾熱情與接受度超乎預期。
從挑戰者轉變為尋求連任者，鄭世維形容，蔣萬安沒變的是謀定而後動、務實勤懇的性格。
戴錫欽則透露，蔣萬安私下像大男孩，與各年齡層都能打成一片，在選戰高壓下，還能針對不同對象展現幽默一面。
幕僚表示，蔣萬安的個性謙和但有主見，同時也尊重他人、照顧他人感受，行程繁忙仍經常找空檔關心基層的工作狀況，當蔣萬安看見問題，就不會置之不理，「他是會把問題放在心上的人」。
幕僚認為，蔣萬安個性溫柔，但領導、推動市政的態度堅毅，「他很常講的一句話是對的事情就要堅持去做、勇敢去做」，以拆除公館圓環為例，經地方溝通、專業評估認定是「對的方向」，蔣萬安就會帶領團隊堅定推行。
此外，無論是競選辦公室或市府發言團隊，蔣萬安多任用年輕人，顯見其重視團隊多元組成。幕僚說，市政會議時，蔣萬安除聽取各局處專業分析，也重視發言團隊想法，平時在市府內遇到幕僚，他也會停下來多聊兩句，聆聽團隊針對時事議題的意見。
身為爭取連任者，蔣萬安多次強調「市政優先」，拋出松山機場遷建，打造台北AI園區；放寬都市更新門檻，有條件提高基準容積等政見，也暢談過去4年的施政成果，包括大巨蛋完工啟用、輝達海外總部落腳台北等，盼以政績說服市民。
曾為國民黨贏回台北市的蔣萬安，在這次選戰中多次強調他「說到做到」，把對選民承諾化為具體行動，盼用4年實績、親切態度證明自己值得市民再次託付，讓他在現有市政基礎下擘劃台北願景、持續前行。（編輯：蕭博文）1151122

content:
资料照片：一架空客A350飞机准备在阿拉伯联合酋长国迪拜航展上降落。(2023年11月14日)
众议院美国与中国共产党战略竞争特设委员会主席约翰·穆勒纳尔(John Moolenaar)星期四(11月19日)公布了该委员会的新调查报告，指出美欧航空航天公司与中国合作对美国国家安全构成的威胁。报告建议美国政府不要认证中国制造的飞机，而如果国防承包商不停止对中国空天产业的投资，美国政府应取消与这些企业的合同。
该特设委员会的这份报告题为《中国的僚机：西方政府政策如何助力中国腾空而起》。(China’s Wingmen: How Western Government Policy Enabled China’s Rise in the Skies)。
“欧美企业向中国转让了技术，这些技术可能会被用来对付我们英勇的男女军人。在中国，由于中国共产党推行‘军民融合’政策，实际上并不存在真正的私营企业。中国人民解放军会利用民用技术来推进其军事野心，这正是此间发生的情况，”穆勒纳尔在声明中说。“美国及其盟友应加强对航空航天领域的出口管制与投资限制，以阻止转让关键技术，避免助力我们最主要的敌手。”
西方航空航天企业通过合法商业安排，将先进技术知识转移给了中国航空航天企业。
霍尼韦尔(Honeywell)、通用电气航空(GE Aerospace)和柯林斯(Collins)多次申请并获得了转让受管控技术的许可，涉及中国境内的军事最终用户及其他与军方有关联的商业航空航天实体。
美国的出口管制在很大程度上依赖于企业自身尽职调查，然而，商业利益往往倾向于维持既有合作，而以前的执法行动已暴露出企业在合规方面的薄弱环节。
在中国境内设立的合资企业，使敏感技术得以转移境外，避开美国外国投资委员会(CFIUS)审查框架，从而在美国国家安全审查机制中造成了一个结构性的漏洞。
如果美国采取单边限制措施，不仅会使美国的航空航天企业处于不利地位，而且也无法真正阻止中国获取各类西方技术，因为盟国企业往往会趁机填补市场空缺。
如果某些企业打造敌手的军事能力并使这些能力可能被转而用于针对美国及其盟友，美国纳税人的钱就不应投入到这些企业。
美国财政部应在其“对外投资安全计划”(Outbound Investment Security Program)框架下，限制对中国航空航天领域的投资，国会则应通过修订《2025年全面对外投资国家安全法案》（COINS法案），将这一禁令以法律形式固定下来。
美国联邦航空管理局(FAA)不应为中国制造的航空器进行适航认证。
国会应通过《航空航天透明度法案》(H.R. 11047)，要求与美国战争部开展业务的航空航天承包商披露其与美国所认定的中国军事企业之间的关联，从而使战争部能够掌握必要信息，以评估并应对这些关联所带来的风险。
美国国务院和商务部应彻底重审航空航天技术许可的管理方式：全面减少对敌手的技术出口，要求所有相关方充分披露其最终受益所有权(beneficial ownership)，禁止出口具有军民两用性质的技术，或禁止出口可能被中国军事企业获取的技术；并对违规行为实施具有实质威慑力的惩罚措施。
国会应通过《地理空间情报透明度与安全法案》（H.R. 11048），责成美国国家地理空间情报局(NGA)全面评估商业地理空间超级智能能力的发展状况，识别出其中对国家安全构成最大威胁的部分，并将评估结果通报给商务部和国务院，以便为制定出口管制规则及开展国际谈判提供参考。
对于法国企业拟收购美国航空航天公司的行为，应实施更严格的审查，在这些法国企业切断与中国“军民融合”生态系统的联系之前，应预设不予批准此类收购。
这份调查报告还随附了一封该委员会给总部位于法国的欧洲民航飞机制造巨头空中客车(Airbus)负责人的信函，要求就空客与中国航空工业集团(AVIC)持续存在的合作关系进行对话并索取更多信息。
该特设委员会对空客公司与中国的各项合作关系，包括帮助中国军方开发直-15直升机以及与中国商飞(COMAC)合作开发能与空客飞机竞争的产品表达了关切。
这封信说：“过去25年里，美国政府和国会曾基于一种天真的假设行事，那就是：强劲的经济接触会促使中国共产党走向政治自由化。为了推进这一错误的战略目标，美国政府鼓励包括空中客车在内的企业在中华人民共和国进行大规模投资。全球潜在最大市场的前景曾被形容为一个巨大的机遇。然而，情况已经发生了改变。”
这封信接着说：“一旦美国政府最终认识到中共构成的威胁，美国对中国的错误乐观就转变成为清醒正视。随着国会和美国政府将其做法转变为正视这一生存威胁，我们期待企业真诚地与我们合作，解除损害美国国家安全的关系。”

F-35C 在福特级航母上完成首次发射和回收试验 - 国防新闻
F-35C 在福特级航母上完成首次发射和回收试验

2026 年 11 月 2 日，一架 F-35C 闪电 II 从未来的约翰·肯尼迪号飞机上起飞。（洛克希德·马丁公司）
洛克希德·马丁公司周四表示，两架海军 F-35C 闪电 II 战斗机已在未来的美国海军第二艘杰拉尔德·R·福特级航空母舰约翰·F·肯尼迪号上完成了该机的第一轮发射和回收测试。
该公司表示，从 10 月 13 日（海军成立 251 周年）开始的 11 天测试中，这两架飞机进行了 34 次飞行，记录了 122 次弹射器发射和 122 次拦截着陆。这架飞机隶属于马里兰州帕图森特河海军航空站的第 23 空中测试和评估中队（VX-23），被称为“咸狗”。
据海军称，这些飞行是肯尼迪飞机兼容性测试的一部分，该测试评估该舰的发射和回收设备如何与海军飞机配合使用。海军照片说明显示，第一次拦截着陆发生在 10 月 13 日，第一次弹射器发射发生在 10 月 14 日。
与使用蒸汽弹射器和液压拦阻装置发射和回收飞机的尼米兹级航母不同，福特级航母使用电磁飞机发射系统（EMALS）和先进拦阻装置（AAG）。洛克希德公司表示，EMALS 可以实现更平稳、更精确控制的发射，而 AAG 可以处理更广泛的回收条件。
福特级还有一个较小的岛，即装有舰桥和飞行控制系统的塔，其位置比尼米兹级舰向后约 140 英尺。洛克希德公司表示，该岛和重新设计的飞行甲板改变了气流、排气模式和甲板操作。
该公司表示，此次海上测试是在 2024 年 1 月至 2025 年 5 月进行的岸基试验之后进行的。它验证了飞机的结构模型，并验证了 EMALS 和 AAG 背后的软件和设备。这些数据将有助于开发福特级船舶上使用的发射和回收指导人员。
洛克希德·马丁公司 F-35 开发项目副总裁肖恩·杰克逊 (Sean Jackson) 表示：“这对于 F-35C、肯尼迪和美国海军来说都是一个关键事件。” “这架飞机首次在杰拉尔德·R·福特级飞行甲板上演示了发射和回收操作，推动了第五代战斗机能力与世界最先进航母技术的融合。”
杰克逊还表示，在完成这一测试阶段后，“海军现已批准 F-35C 在其整个航空母舰舰队中运行。”
洛克希德公司的一名官员告诉《防务新闻》：“一旦发射和回收公告发布，这些舰艇就可以发射和回收 F-35。” “在配套设备齐全之前，他们不会做好部署准备。”
这位官员补充说，海军已获得“最终许可”。
F-35C 于 2014 年 11 月在圣地亚哥附近的尼米兹号航空母舰上首次降落在航母上，此后一直在改装的尼米兹级航母上部署。福特级的主舰杰拉尔德·R·福特号航空母舰尚未与该喷气式飞机一起部署。
2019 年，海军发言人告诉 USNI 新闻，这两个航母级别都可以使用 F-35C 作战

F-35C completes first launch and recovery trials on a Ford-class carrier

A F-35C Lightning II takes off from the future John F. Kennedy, Nov. 2, 2026. (Lockheed Martin)
Two Navy F-35C Lightning II fighters have completed the jet’s first round of launch and recovery testing aboard the future USS John F. Kennedy, the Navy’s second Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, Lockheed Martin said Thursday.
Over 11 days of testing that began Oct. 13, the Navy’s 251st birthday, the two jets made 34 flights and logged 122 catapult launches and 122 arrested landings, the company said. The aircraft belong to Air Test and Evaluation Squadron 23, or VX-23, known as the “Salty Dogs,” at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland.
The flights were part of Kennedy’s Aircraft Compatibility Testing, which assesses how the ship’s launch and recovery equipment works with Navy aircraft, according to the Navy. The first arrested landing came on Oct. 13, and the first catapult launch on Oct. 14, Navy photo captions show.
Unlike Nimitz-class carriers, which launch and recover aircraft with steam catapults and hydraulic arresting gear, Ford-class carriers use the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System, or EMALS, and the Advanced Arresting Gear, or AAG. Lockheed said EMALS allows smoother, more precisely controlled launches, while AAG can handle a broader range of recovery conditions.
The Ford class also has a smaller island, the tower that houses the bridge and flight control, set about 140 feet farther back than on Nimitz-class ships. Lockheed said the island and a redesigned flight deck change airflow, exhaust patterns and deck operations.
The at-sea testing followed shore-based trials conducted from January 2024 to May 2025, the company said. It validated the jet’s structural models and verified the software and equipment behind EMALS and AAG. The data will help develop the launch and recovery guidance crews use on Ford-class ships.
“This is a critical event for the F-35C, Kennedy, and the United States Navy,” said Sean Jackson, vice president of Lockheed Martin’s F-35 Development Program. “For the first time, the aircraft has demonstrated launch and recovery operations from a Gerald R. Ford-Class flight deck, advancing the integration of fifth-generation fighter capability with the world’s most advanced carrier technology.”
Jackson also said that upon completion of this test phase, “the Navy has now cleared the F-35C for operations across its entire fleet of aircraft carriers.”
“The ships are cleared to launch and recover F-35s once the launch and recovery bulletins are published,” a Lockheed official told Defense News. “They will not be ready to deploy until fully outfitted with supporting equipment.”
The Navy, the official added, has the “final clearance.”
The F-35C first landed on a carrier in November 2014, aboard USS Nimitz off San Diego, and has since deployed from modified Nimitz-class carriers. The lead ship of the Ford class, USS Gerald R. Ford, has not deployed with the jet.
In 2019, a Navy spokesman told USNI News that both carrier classes could operate with F-35Cs by design but needed changes, such as more robust jet blast deflectors and classified spaces, for the jet to be more effective on a full-length deployment. Stars and Stripes reported in October that the Navy plans to retrofit the Ford to operate the F-35C.
Kennedy received those modifications during construction. In 2020, the Navy changed the ship’s construction contract to meet a legislative requirement that Kennedy be capable of deploying with the F-35C.
The Navy took preliminary acceptance of Kennedy on Sept. 29, after the ship completed acceptance trials in August. Preliminary acceptance allows the crew to test and train at sea while the shipbuilder finishes its work. The Navy said at the time that the ship was about 99% complete, and formal delivery is planned for spring 2027.
Michael Scanlon is a defense journalist covering air and space warfare. A former U.S. Air Force A-10 crew chief, he has supported land and sea programs for the U.S. Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Coast Guard.

content:
台湾两党瞄准关键战场 地方选举前最后冲刺 - 聚焦台湾
2026年选举/台湾各党派瞄准关键战场，为地方选举前的最后冲刺
要激活文字转语音服务，请首先同意以下隐私政策。
副总统萧美琴（右）为苏教蕙（右二）竞选，新北市长侯裕义（左二）为李树全（左）竞选。 CNA 合成照片
中新社台北11月21日电 台湾两大政党派出最高竞选人士前往台北和新北举行选举前夕集会，寻求在下周六地方选举之前扩大或捍卫其在关键战场地区的政治立足点。
执政的民进党（民进党）在台湾六个直辖市中仅统治台南和高雄，它希望推翻台北、新北和台中，人们认为在这些地方它的机会比桃园更大。
一位党内消息人士告诉中央社，选举前夕，总统赖清德和前总统蔡英文将竞选该党的市长候选人：台北市长候选人沉伯洋和新北市长候选人苏巧慧。
周六，前总统蔡英文（右）为执政的民进党新北市长候选人苏娇晖（左）竞选。中央通讯社照片2026年11月21日
副总统萧美琴和行政院长卓荣泰将出席台中市长候选人何欣纯的集会。
与此同时，一位党内消息人士称，主要反对党国民党将把最后的竞选努力集中在确保台北市市长蒋万安连任以及新北候选人李四川的胜利上。
国民党主席郑丽文近日向镜报表示，台北、新北、桃园和台中的市长选举竞争激烈，但她对国民党在这四个城市的胜算仍持乐观态度。
一名党内消息人士告诉中央社，李光耀和桃园市长张善政预计将参加蒋介石的选举前夕集会，以展示党内团结，并敦促全国各地的支持者支持国民党候选人。
台湾22个市县中，国民党管辖15个，民进党管辖5个。新竹市由前台湾人民党（TPP）的独立市长高虹安领导，而金门县也由独立人士管辖。
民进党消息人士称，该党的目标是保住嘉义县、屏东县、澎湖县，以及台南县和高雄县，但没有透露其认为可以获胜的其他市县。
不过，消息人士指出，台中和基隆是关键战场。
据国民党消息人士透露，除了六个直辖市外，国民党在宜兰县、彰化县、新竹县以及基隆市面临着更艰难的竞选。
国民党表示，立法院院长韩国瑜、台中市长卢秀燕、新北市长侯友宜将在大选前最后一周加紧拉选党内候选人。
现任国民党台北市市长蒋万安（中）的竞选海报展示了台中市市长卢秀岩（左）和立法院院长韩国瑜（右）。蒋万安竞选办公室供图
至于小反对党TPP，其在全国市长和县长竞选中唯一的候选人是在国民党支持下竞选嘉义市市长的张启楷。
